## Arch Framework Slope Mould Buyer Guide

Straight ribs, radius-specific curved beams and numbered set pieces for highway, railway and dam arch slope protection.

## Four mould groups on this page

- Straight arch beams: flat ribs and crosspieces, 42×8×8cm up to 73×30×10cm. Interchangeable by length and thickness — order by running length.

- Curved arch beams: the arc of each ring, radius-specific from R75 to R225. One mould = one radius; count them per ring.

- Complete set pieces: lettered A–H or numbered 1#–5# (incl. left/right) pieces forming one arch ring of inner Ø2.5m or Ø3m, in 15/20/25cm thickness.

- L-type side beams & frame-grid blocks: outer edge L-beams and the square frame-grid (31×31×15cm) + strip-stone lattice alternative.

## Three things buyers get wrong

- Ordering curved beams by size only. The R radius is locked by the arch drawing — same size, wrong radius will not assemble. Always quote R.

- Mixing set pieces across diameters. A piece from a Ø3m set does not fit a Ø2.5m ring; order complete sets per ring and multiply by ring count, with breakage spares.

- Under-counting curved beams. They cannot be replaced by straight beams on site. Count rings × curved pieces per ring before ordering.

Project needRecommended mould directionQuote details to prepare

Arch framework for highway/railway slopeComplete set (pieces A–H / No.1–5) + curved beams by radiusInner arch diameter, beam width/thickness, piece list, R value

Long slope run, many identical ringsFull set per ring × ring count + spare curved piecesSlope length, ring spacing, rings per slope, spare %

Lattice / frame-grid slope instead of archesFrame-grid block 31×31×15cm + strip stones + L-type edge beamsGrid spacing, strip-stone lengths, edge beam section

## Arch Framework Slope Mould FAQ

## What is an arch framework slope protection system?
Arch framework (gongxing gujia) slope protection is a reinforced concrete grid of arched ribs cast on highway, railway and dam slopes. Concrete arch beams interlock into rings that trap soil and vegetation; the arched shape transfers slope load into the side beams. It is one of the most common engineered slope systems for long transport cuts and embankments. We mould every piece: straight beams, curved arch beams, and the numbered or lettered set pieces.

## Why do curved arch beams have an R value, and why does it matter?
R is the arc radius of the curved beam in centimetres — we carry R75, R100, R120, R122, R125, R150, R200 and R225. One curved-beam mould makes one radius only, exactly like curved kerbstone: an R150 beam cannot be bent to R120 on site. The radius is fixed by the arch drawing and the inner arch diameter, so quote the R from the drawing, not from an existing beam. Ordering the wrong R is the most common mistake because straight and curved beams of the same nominal size look similar in photos.

## What does 'inner Ø3m' or 'inner Ø2.5m' mean for a complete set?
It is the clear inside diameter of each arch ring after assembly. A set is made of several numbered pieces (A–H or No.1–No.5, with left/right handed variants) that together form one ring. Pieces are not interchangeable between diameters: a No.2 piece from a Ø3m set does not fit a Ø2.5m ring. Common set thicknesses are 15, 20 and 25cm. Buy by the complete set per ring, and multiply by the number of rings along the slope plus spare pieces for breakage.

## How do I order a complete arch framework set correctly?
Send the arch design drawing (or the standard the project references) with: inner arch diameter, beam width and thickness, the number of pieces per ring and their numbers, the curved-beam radius, and the L-type side beam size. The Fujian and Anhui highway sets we hold are R150/R125 reference designs — if your project matches a regional standard, name it and we can map pieces directly.

## Straight beams versus curved beams — which and how many?
Straight beams (the flat ribs and crosspieces) are interchangeable by length and thickness, so order those by running length. Curved beams are radius-specific and used per arch ring, so count rings × curved pieces per ring and add spares. Under-ordering curved beams is the usual cause of a half-finished slope because they cannot be substituted with straight ones.

## Do you supply the frame-grid (kuangge) slope blocks too?
Yes. The square frame-grid block (31×31×15cm) and its strip stones (100×10×15cm, 79×10×15cm) form the alternative lattice-slope system, and L-type side edge beams (e.g. 49.5×41×16cm) finish the outer edges. These can be ordered with the arch system so the whole slope face is cast from matched moulds.

## What material and how many pours do these moulds last?
Straight and simple curved beams use polypropylene (PP) for 150+ pour cycles with good demoulding flexibility. Large set pieces and tight-radius curved beams are often made in ABS for crisper, dimensionally stable arcs over many cycles. We recommend PP/ABS based on the piece and your volume.

## What is the MOQ and lead time for arch framework moulds?
Mixed-SKU orders are welcome; there is no strict MOQ on catalogue beams. Complete multi-piece sets are made to order and typically run 15–30 days after the arch drawing is approved. Because sets are long and bulky, we plan container loading in advance (20'/40' HQ, flat-rack or open-top). Send the drawing, quantities per piece and destination port for an FOB Ningbo/Shanghai quote.

# Product: Breeze Block & Decorative Screen Block Moulds

## Moulds for Decorative Screen Walls and Ventilated Facades
Breeze blocks — also called decorative screen blocks, ventilation blocks or jali blocks — are perforated concrete units used to build screen walls, privacy partitions, ventilated facades, garden walls and balcony infills. They provide shade and airflow while keeping a strong architectural pattern.
Zhihua supplies moulds for 48 pattern designs across 20×20×6cm, 25×25×6cm, 30×30×7cm, 32×32×10cm, 34×34×6cm and 40×40×7cm formats, including three-in-one mini blocks and framed decorative units. OEM patterns can be produced from drawings or sample photos.

## Breeze Block Mould Buyer Guide

Breeze block mould selection is driven by the block face size, thickness and pattern, plus whether the wall is load-bearing infill or purely a decorative screen.

## Typical breeze block formats

- 20×20×6cm: the most widely used screen block size, 26 pattern designs available.

- 30×30×7cm: larger face for feature walls and faster wall build-up, 18 designs available.

- 25×25 – 34×34cm: intermediate formats including 32×32×10cm thick blocks and square fret patterns.

- 40×40×7cm: large-format screen block for high walls and facade panels.

## Project drawing checklist

For breeze block moulds, the key parameters are block face dimensions, thickness and the pattern opening geometry. A photo of the reference wall helps us match the design.

- Confirm block face size and thickness (e.g. 20×20×6cm).

- Send a photo or drawing of the required pattern.

- State whether blocks are stacked dry, mortared or reinforced.

ApplicationSuitable mould typeKey parameters

Privacy screen wall20×20×6cm patterned blocksFace size, pattern openness, thickness
Feature / facade wall30×30×7cm and 40×40×7cm blocksFace size, pattern repeat, thickness
Thick structural screen32×32×10cm and 30×30×12cm blocksThickness, hole geometry, reinforcement path

## What to send for a fast quote
Breeze block projects are usually driven by an architectural reference image. A photo of the target wall plus block dimensions lets us match a catalogue pattern or quote an OEM mould.

- Block face dimensions and thickness

- Pattern reference photo, drawing or catalogue number

- Wall area in square metres and required block quantity

- Destination country and whether mixed patterns are needed

## Need breeze block moulds for a project?
Send your drawing or a photo of the target result. We can review catalogue options or OEM mould feasibility.

## Breeze Block Moulds in the Workshop

Grid, cross and square-cell screen block patterns, filmed on our own injection moulding line. If you need a pattern or block size that is not on this page, send a drawing or a photo with dimensions and we will check it against our tooling.

## The Breeze Block Pattern Library — Two-Sided Smooth Moulds

Eight-plus decorative hollow block patterns in one aisle. Both faces of each block come out smooth (no render needed). Send a sketch or CAD and we can cut a custom pattern in 10-15 days.

## Breeze Block Mould FAQ

## What is a breeze block used for?
Breeze blocks are perforated concrete units used for screen walls, privacy partitions, ventilated facades, garden walls and balcony infills. They allow airflow and light while forming a decorative pattern.

## How many breeze block patterns do you have?
We currently offer 48 pattern designs across 20×20, 25×25, 30×30, 32×32, 34×34 and 40×40cm formats. Additional patterns can be produced as OEM moulds.

## Can you make a custom breeze block pattern?
Yes. Send a drawing, CAD file or photo of the pattern. We can review mould feasibility, draft angles and demoulding direction, then quote OEM production.

## Road Shoulder Stone & Bridge Cap Mould Buyer Guide

Highway shoulder stones, sloped/perforated edge stones, retaining blocks and bridge cap coping — match the mould to the finished cross-section, drainage and load.

## Four mould groups on this page

- Road shoulder stones: flat edge stones 49.5–60cm long, 8–26cm thick, for the pavement-to-shoulder edge.

- Perforated / sloped / beveled: stones with a pitched top, chamfered face, or moulded drain hole (1-hole, half-round Ø19) for edge drainage.

- Cover slabs, retaining & notched pieces: shoulder cover slabs (13.8cm), tall retaining blocks (36.7cm) and left/right notched end units.

- Bridge caps & L-caps: thick coping caps (50–60cm wide, 20–33.5cm high) for piers/abutments, plus L-shaped corner caps.

## Three things buyers get wrong

- Confusing shoulder stones with bridge caps. They share a photo style but are different units — thin drainage edge stone vs thick structural coping cap. Order from the cross-section drawing, not the name alone.

- Treating left/right notched pieces as interchangeable. On a sloped stone the notch hand is fixed; count right-notch and left-notch separately.

- Planning to drill holes or cut bevels after casting. Holes and slopes are moulded in; drilling/chiselling cured concrete chips the face and weakens the edge.

Project needRecommended mould directionQuote details to prepare

Highway pavement edgeFlat or sloped road shoulder stone mouldLength × width × thickness, flat or sloped/beveled top

Edge drainage through the shoulder1-hole / half-round-hole / perforated sloped shoulder stoneHole size & position, slope pitch, run spacing

Shoulder trench or edge drain capShoulder cover slab + tall retaining block mouldCover size, retaining block height & sloped face

Bridge pier / abutment copingBridge cap or L-shaped cap mould (ABS for depth)Cap width × height × length, L-shape wrap, reinforcement

## Road Shoulder Stone & Bridge Cap Mould FAQ

## What is the difference between a road shoulder stone and a bridge cap (taimao)?
Road shoulder stones (路肩石) are the edge blocks along a highway shoulder — typically 49.5–75cm long, 8–26cm thick, flat or sloped/beveled on top, sometimes with a drain hole or an end notch. They separate the pavement from the shoulder and carry edge drainage. Bridge caps / taimao (台帽) are the thicker coping blocks (30–41cm wide, 20–33.5cm high) that sit on top of bridge piers, abutments or retaining-wall posts as a load-distribution cap; L-shaped caps (L型台帽) wrap a corner. They are heavier structural units, not drainage edge stones.

## What do sloped, beveled and flat shoulder stones mean?
Flat shoulder stones (平石) have a level top. Sloped (坡型) stones have a pitched top that sheds water off the pavement; beveled (斜面) stones have a chamfered face (e.g. a 14cm bevel on the 50×50×15). The slope/bevel is cast into the mould and is not cut afterwards, so quote the finished cross-section drawing. Perforated versions (1-hole, half-round Ø19 hole, perforated sloped) drain through the stone.

## How do the notched shoulder stone pieces fit?
Notched pieces (缺口1 right notch, 缺口2 left notch on the 55×50×10.3 stone) are end units with a side opening that lets water or an adjacent block interlock at a node. Left and right are separate moulds — order them by hand and count, since a right-notch piece cannot be flipped to make a left-notch run when the top is sloped.

## Are the drain holes drilled on site?
No. The 1-hole, half-round-hole (Ø19) and perforated sloped shoulder stones are moulded with the hole as part of the concrete shape. Give the hole size and position; each layout is a separate mould. Do not drill cured stones — it chips the sloped face and weakens the edge.

## What are the retaining block and shoulder cover slab for?
The retaining block (挡土块, 50×35×36.7 with a 20cm sloped face) is a tall shoulder unit that holds back fill at the pavement edge. The shoulder cover slab (路肩盖板, 50×49×13.8) caps a shoulder trench or edge drain. These work with the flat and sloped shoulder stones to finish the edge and its drainage.

## PP or ABS for shoulder and cap moulds?
Thin flat shoulder stones (8–10cm) demould well in PP for 150+ pour cycles. Thick bridge caps (up to 33.5cm high) and L-shaped corner caps with deep right-angle sections are better in ABS for stiffness and dimensional stability over heavy pours. We recommend material based on the section depth.

## What concrete grade and reinforcement do these need?
C25–C30 concrete with vibration and curing for standard shoulder stones. Bridge caps and tall retaining blocks that distribute pier or backfill load should use higher-grade reinforced concrete per the bridge design — the mould accommodates rebar cages. Note that load capacity is a property of the concrete, reinforcement and section, not of the mould.

## What is the MOQ and lead time?
Mixed-SKU orders are welcome with no strict MOQ on catalogue sizes. Custom sections, bevels, hole layouts or L-shaped caps are made to order, typically 15–30 days after drawing approval. Bridge cap moulds are bulky; we plan container loading for 40'HQ. Send drawings, quantities and destination port for an FOB Ningbo/Shanghai quote.

## Cable Trench Cover Mould Buyer Guide

Choose cable trench covers by the trench clear opening, seat width, required thickness/load environment, how often crews need to lift the slab (lift-handle vs fixed) and whether the project is a substation, metro or tunnel.

## Common cable trench mould choices

- U-shaped cable trench moulds: open concrete cable channels for power, telecom and industrial utility lines.

- Deep utility trench moulds: larger components for cable protection, inspection and repeated installation dimensions.

- Trench cover moulds: matching covers with holes, ribs or anti-slip patterns.

- Double-slot duct moulds: used when different cable or service lines need separation.

## Engineering details that matter

For cover moulds, the seat detail, notch, lifting-hole positions, tread pattern and slab thickness decide whether the finished concrete cover seats correctly and can be lifted safely.

- Provide inside and outside dimensions if available.

- Confirm whether the trench needs a separate cover mould.

- Tell us if the product is for power, telecom, railway, substation or municipal corridor use.

## Cable Trench Cover Moulds FAQ

## Are these cable trench body moulds or cover moulds?
This page is our cable trench COVER programme — removable lift-handle (提手) covers that seat on top of a concrete or brick cable trench, plus metro and tunnel trough covers. We supply the cover moulds; if you also need the U-shaped trench body mould, those are quoted separately from your section drawing (see our Drainage Channel / U-channel range).

## What is a lift-handle (提手) cover and why use one?
A lift-handle cover has moulded lifting slots or pull points (e.g. 8.5×3.5cm slots) so maintenance crews can lift the slab to pull or inspect power/telecom cables, then seat it flush again — no cast-in iron frame needed. It is the standard removable cover for substations, industrial parks and utility corridors.

## Which size fits my cable trench — 80×50, 138×40 or 170×50?
The cover size is set by your trench clear opening plus the seat/bearing width on each side, not by the trench width alone. A 170×50cm cover, for example, typically seats over a narrower trench. Send the trench inner width, wall/seat width and required cover thickness and we will match the mould.

## PP or ABS for cable trench covers?
PP (polypropylene) is the lower-cost choice for standard lift covers up to ~80cm and high-cycle yard production. Use ABS for large 100–170cm panels, deep 20–26cm tunnel sections and metro/T-junction assembly sets, where extra rigidity and demoulding stiffness matter.

## Can the cover have a notch, drainage slots or an anti-slip tread?
Yes — notches (e.g. 20×1cm frame-clearance notch), lifting holes, drainage slots and cobblestone/striped anti-slip treads are all moulded directly into the part. A notch must be moulded, not cut on site, or it will crack under load.

## What are the metro T-junction assembly and deep-burial tunnel covers?
For subway and tunnel troughs we supply multi-part assembly sets (e.g. the 60.8×59×34.4cm T-junction set, supplied with a demoulding diagram) and ultra-thick 20–26cm deep-burial covers (60×50×26, 85×49×20). These are engineered to railway/metro drawings and quoted as sets.

## Do you quote load ratings for the covers?
We do not stamp a load class on the mould — load capacity is a property of the finished reinforced concrete (rebar design, concrete grade and cover thickness). We provide the mould geometry and wall/rib design to your drawing; the structural rating is set by the precaster's concrete design.

## Can you make cable trench covers from our project drawings?
Yes. Send the finished cover drawing (length × width × thickness), seat/notch detail, lifting-hole or handle positions, tread pattern and material preference (PP/ABS). We confirm whether it matches existing tooling or needs a new OEM mould before quotation.

## Cobblestone Cover Mould Buyer Guide

The cobblestone pattern is a surface finish — the same texture is made in thin 2.5–5cm pedestrian panels and thick 6–10cm railway-standard covers. Pick the cover type by what the trench carries and the load on top.

## Six cover groups on this page

- Plain solid covers: fully close the trench; 6–8.3cm for cable trenches and roadside ditches (33 moulds, 29.4–179cm).

- Notched covers: edge cut-out for a pipe/cable crossing — middle-notched or end-notched; quote the notch size (12 moulds).

- 2-hole / 4-hole perforated: drainage openings for trenches that carry stormwater (6 moulds).

- Railway-standard (铁标 Tie Biao): thick 5–8cm track-side covers, long narrow 19–24cm widths, often ABS (8 moulds).

- Thin pedestrian panels: 2.5–5cm for footpaths, gardens and plazas; large thin panels in ABS for stiffness (14 moulds).

- Walkway / step / curved / metro-platform slabs: long narrow 步板 walking plates, curved ramp slabs and the one-mould-three-width metro evacuation-platform plate (9 moulds).

## Three things buyers get wrong

- Assuming 'cobblestone' means decorative / light duty. The pattern is cosmetic; thickness and reinforcement set the load. The same texture is supplied as 2.5cm garden panels and 8cm railway covers.

- Ordering a plain cover where a pipe crosses the trench. Use a notched (缺口) cover at the crossing and quote the notch size (e.g. 20×1.5, 30×1.5, 40×2.5cm) and middle-vs-end position — a site-cut notch destroys the cover edge.

- Using PP for a large thin panel. Big 2.5–3.5cm panels (e.g. 75×50×3.5, 121.5×50×3) flex in PP; these are moulded in ABS to stay flat, as are railway-standard covers.

ApplicationCover type & typical thicknessQuote details to prepare

Garden paths, parks, plazas (pedestrian)Plain thin cobblestone panel, 2.5–5cmL×W×T, pattern, area / linear metres

Municipal roadside ditch / cable trenchPlain or perforated, 6–8.3cmL×W×T, solid vs 2-hole/4-hole, load

Pipe / cable crossing pointNotched cover (middle or end), 6–10cmL×W×T, notch dimensions, notch position

High-speed-rail / metro track-sideRailway-standard (铁标), walkway/step slabs, 7–8cmProject standard / drawing, PP or ABS

## Cobblestone Cover Moulds Fresh From the Injection Machine, 20×15 Notch

Pebble-texture covers straight off the machine — cobblestone pattern is decorative and anti-slip, and the 20×15 cm notched edge lets covers interlock over the trench. Order by trench clear span, not outer size.

## Large Cobblestone Drainage Cover Mould 82.6×49.6×7.3 cm | Pebble Pattern

The oversized version — 82.6×49.6×7.3 cm alongside a 57.6×49.6×7.3 cm one. A 7.3 cm section this size is for vehicle-access areas, and the back rib grid is what keeps a cover over 60 cm flat.

## Cobblestone Drainage Cover Mould FAQ

## What is a cobblestone-pattern drainage cover mould?
It is a plastic (PP/ABS) injection mould that casts a concrete trench or ditch cover with a raised cobblestone/pebble surface (鹅卵石花纹). The finished cover is a functional drain cover for cable trenches, roadside ditches and landscape channels, but the cobblestone texture looks like stone paving and adds slip resistance — so it is widely used in parks, garden paths, residential communities and municipal 'green' projects where a plain flat cover would look out of place.

## Are these covers only decorative / light duty?
No. The cobblestone pattern is a surface finish, not a sign of light duty. The same pattern is made in thin 2.5–5cm pedestrian panels for garden paths AND in thick 6–10cm heavy-duty covers, including 铁标 (railway-standard, 'Tie Biao') covers for high-speed-rail and metro cable trenches that are walked on by maintenance crews. Load capacity is set by thickness and reinforcement, not by the pattern. Tell us the application (footpath / roadside / track-side) and we recommend the thickness.

## What is the difference between plain, notched and 2-hole/4-hole covers?
Plain (solid) covers fully close the trench. Notched covers (缺口盖板) have a cut-out on one edge where a pipe or cable crosses the trench — there are middle-notched and end-notched versions; quote the notch size (e.g. 20×1.5cm or 30×1.5cm) and whether it is on the middle of a run or at the end. 2-hole / 4-hole covers (二孔/四孔) have drainage openings for higher stormwater flow, used where the trench itself drains surface water. Choose by whether the trench carries cables (solid/notched) or water (perforated).

## What are railway-standard (铁标 / Tie Biao) cobblestone covers?
These are covers produced to Chinese railway-project standards, often marked '铁标' and a factory/source mark such as '广工' (Guang Gong). They are used along high-speed-rail and metro lines for cable-trench covers and walkway slabs — typically the long narrow sizes (e.g. 98×19, 98×24, 148×19, 152×24cm) in thicker 7–8cm sections, moulded in ABS or heavy PP for stiffness and long service. We can produce to a railway project drawing or standard; send the spec sheet or project standard.

## What are the walkway slabs and curved / metro platform plates?
The long narrow walkway/step slabs (步板, e.g. 98×25×8, 98×50×8, 158×25×8) are the walking-surface plates along track-side and cable trenches. Curved walkway/step slabs (弧形踏步板/步行板, e.g. the Zheng-Fu high-speed-rail items, 86×73.5/61cm and 73×61×30cm) follow a curved or ramped trench alignment. The metro evacuation-platform plate (地铁疏散平台, 99cm) is a special one-mould-three-width plate producing 24.5/19.5/14.5/9.5cm widths from a single mould set — quote the platform cross-section.

## How do I specify a custom or project cover (Jing-Zhang, Yunping, Weilai, CECEP)?
Many of these covers were made for named projects — e.g. Jing-Zhang HSR (京张, thin 44.4×49.4×2.8), Yunping expressway (云平高速, notched 71×49×8), Weilai HSR (潍莱, 95×30×6), CECEP (中国节能, 170×50×4). For your own project send: the cover length × width × thickness, whether it is plain/notched/perforated (with notch or hole dimensions), the load/application, the required surface pattern, and any standard it must meet. We confirm the mould design and demoulding before tooling.

## Which material — PP or ABS — and how many pours?
Standard 6–8cm covers in PP give 150+ pour cycles and are the economical choice for most landscape and municipal runs. ABS is used for the thin stiff panels (2.5–5cm large-format covers like 75×50×3.5 and 121.5×50×3, which would flex in PP), for railway-standard covers, and for deeply-profiled cobblestone texture that needs sharper detail release. We recommend the material based on size, thickness and pattern depth.

## What about MOQ, lead time and shipping?
Mixed-SKU orders have no strict MOQ — you can combine sizes across the 82 catalogue moulds. Custom project moulds are made to order in roughly 15–30 days after drawing approval. Covers are lightweight injection-moulded plastic (the moulds, not the concrete), so they pack efficiently; send the destination port and we quote FOB Ningbo/Shanghai. WhatsApp us a photo of the cover you want to match and we confirm the nearest catalogue size or quote a custom mould.

## Concrete Post & Marker Pile Mould Buyer Guide

Fence posts, landscape wood-grain piles, railway cable marker piles and wire-mesh boundary posts — match the mould to the post length, section and embossed marking.

## Four mould groups on this page

- Cylindrical columns: round moulds Ø20–21cm, 41–51cm high for short bollards and columns.

- Imitation-wood piles: Ø15/20/25/30cm, 50–150cm long; smooth, wood-grain or tree-grain; pointed or flat; matching wood-grain caps for Ø15/20/30.

- Square posts: 110–260cm long, 10×10 to 25×25cm sections; includes ABS two-section and spliced long posts.

- Marker & wire-mesh posts: plain/triangular marker piles, railway cable marker piles, and wire-mesh fence posts up to 290cm incl. "No Trespassing".

## Three things buyers get wrong

- Ordering a very long post as one mould. Posts over ~2.4m use spliced or two-section moulds — confirm construction so demoulding and joining are planned.

- Forgetting to specify embossed text. Marker-pile wording (cable warning, "No Trespassing", unit name) must be engraved before the mould is cut; it cannot be added to a finished plain pile.

- Mixing pile and cap diameters. The wood-grain cap must match the pile diameter (Ø15/20/30cm); a cap for one size will not seat on another.

## Concrete Post, Pile & Marker Mould FAQ

## What kinds of concrete post and pile moulds are on this page?
Four families: (1) cylindrical round-column moulds (Ø20–21cm, 41–51cm high) for short bollards and columns; (2) imitation-wood landscape pile moulds (仿木桩) in Ø15/20/25/30cm and 50–150cm lengths, smooth, wood-grain or tree-grain, pointed or flat, with matching wood-grain pile caps; (3) square section post moulds from 110 to 260cm long, including an ABS two-section 250×25×25 post and a spliced 260cm post; and (4) marker piles and wire-mesh fence posts — plain or triangular marker piles, railway optical/electric cable marker piles, and wire-mesh fence posts up to 290cm including the 'No Trespassing' (禁止入内) boundary post.

## How are long fence posts moulded — can a 2.9m post come from one mould?
Very long posts use split or spliced moulds. The 260×13.2×10.3cm post is a spliced (拼接) mould and the 250×25×25cm post is a two-section (两段组合) ABS mould; sections align and are cast together or joined per the design. Posts from 110 to 240cm are single-piece. Tell us the target post length and section; we will confirm single-piece vs spliced construction, which affects demoulding and shipping.

## Can marker piles be made with custom embossed text or symbols?
Yes. Marker piles (标志桩) commonly carry warning text, unit names or symbols — for example the railway optical/electric cable marker pile (铁路光缆电缆标志桩) and the 'No Trespassing' (禁止入内) wire-mesh post. Send the required wording, language and logo; the text is engraved into the mould so every cast part carries it. Plain unmarked (无字) marker piles are also standard.

## What is the difference between smooth, wood-grain and pointed imitation-wood piles?
Smooth (光面) piles have a plain concrete surface; wood-grain (木纹) or tree-grain (树纹) piles are cast from a textured mould that looks like timber for landscape and waterfront use; pointed (尖头) piles have a tapered driving end for garden edging, revetment and flower-bed borders. Half-grain versions are smooth on one side and grained on the other. Matching wood-grain pile caps (木纹盖) cap the top for Ø15/20/30cm piles.

## Do the imitation-wood piles need the separate pile cap mould?
The wood-grain cap (仿木桩木纹盖, e.g. 22×19×1.5, 27.5×24×2 or 37.5×34.5×2.5cm) is a separate mould that forms a decorative/driving cap sized to the pile diameter. Order the cap mould in the same diameter as the pile (Ø15/20/30cm). Pointed driving piles usually do not use a cap; flat-topped landscape piles do.

## PP or ABS for these post moulds?
Standard square and round posts demould well in PP for 150+ pour cycles. ABS is used for large or complex sections — the 250×25×25cm two-section post and posts with deep engraved text — where stiffer walls hold dimension over repeated pours. We recommend the material based on the section and your volume.

## What concrete and reinforcement do fence and marker posts need?
C25–C30 concrete with vibration and standard curing. Fence and wire-mesh posts that take mesh or rail loads, and long slender posts (10×10 or 12×12cm sections over 2m), should include rebar or pre-stressed wire; the mould suits reinforced concrete. Marker piles are usually unreinforced or lightly reinforced for roadside burial.

## What is the MOQ, lead time and how are long posts shipped?
Mixed-SKU orders are welcome with no strict MOQ on catalogue posts. Custom-text marker piles and spliced/long posts are made to order, typically 15–30 days after drawing approval. Long post moulds load best in 40'HQ; we plan container loading around the longest piece. Send drawings, quantities, wording and destination port for an FOB Ningbo/Shanghai quote.

# Product: Concrete Rebar Spacer & Cover Block Moulds

## Injection-moulded rebar spacer moulds built for cover accuracy & 150+ pours
Concrete spacer block moulds produce the small elements that sit between rebar and formwork to hold the specified concrete cover thickness. The construction-industry standard for these moulds is injection moulding: molten reinforced polypropylene (PP) or ABS is forced under high pressure into a precision-machined steel cavity, producing a rigid, dimensionally consistent mould with smooth demoulding walls that survives 150+ concrete pour cycles.
Zhihua runs the injection moulding in-house on its own tool shop, so every rebar spacer mould — whether a square/conical/sloped spacer block, a saddle spacer, a bar strip spacer, a plum-blossom rebar cover, a round disc cover or a slot insert — uses a steel tool cut from the buyer's drawing or sample. Standard catalogue items and OEM dimensions are both available.
Buyers searching for injection moulding for rebar spacer, plastic rebar spacer moulds, concrete spacer mould or cover block mould are usually comparing three things: cover-thickness accuracy, 1-out-N count (pieces per pour), and mould service life. All three are locked in at the tool-cutting stage — see the Concrete Spacer Block Moulds Buying Guide for a project checklist.

## Concrete Spacer Block Mould Buyer Guide

Spacer block mould orders are usually driven by rebar cover thickness, mould 1-out-N count and whether the mould is for sloped, saddle, bar strip, plum-blossom or round disc applications.

## Typical spacer mould types

- Spacer block moulds: square, conical, sloped and U-shaped blocks for general cover.

- Saddle spacers: used in slab-on-grade and foundation work to support rebar mesh.

- Bar strip and plum-blossom spacers: for narrow rebar or specific cover thickness requirements.

- Round disc and slot insert spacers: for vertical rebar in columns and walls.

## Project drawing checklist

For spacer block moulds, the key parameters are the cover thickness, finished block dimensions and the 1-out-N count. A sample photo or marked drawing helps confirm orientation and demoulding direction.

- Specify the required cover thickness (e.g. 20mm, 30mm, 50mm).

- Confirm the finished spacer dimensions and 1-out-N count.

- Mark whether the mould is for horizontal slab or vertical rebar use.

ApplicationSuitable mould typeKey parameters

Slab coverSaddle spacers, bar strips, sloped spacer blocksCover thickness, base size, 1-out-N count

Column / wall rebarRound disc covers, slot inserts, plum-blossom coversCover thickness, diameter, rebar diameter compatibility

Foundation / pile capLarge spacer blocks, ballast block mouldsDimensions, load capacity, OEM profile

## Concrete Rebar Spacer Mould FAQ

## Are these rebar spacer moulds injection moulded?
Yes. All Zhihua spacer and cover-block moulds are injection moulded from reinforced polypropylene (PP) or ABS on in-house injection moulding machines using our own steel tools. This is the same process used by major rebar spacer brands worldwide and is what gives the moulds their 150+ pour cycle rating and consistent cover thickness.

## Why injection moulding instead of other plastic processes for rebar spacers?
Injection moulding produces a one-piece, void-free wall with exact cover-thickness tolerance and a smooth interior for clean demoulding. It also allows 1-out-N tools (16/25/36/42/100 cavities per pour), which is the main lever on spacer piece-cost. Thermoformed or 3D-printed moulds cannot match this on either cycle count or dimensional consistency.

## What plastic is used for concrete spacer moulds?
Reinforced polypropylene (PP) is standard for most spacer and cover block moulds because it flexes slightly for demoulding and withstands concrete alkalinity across 150+ cycles. ABS is used for thinner-wall, higher-precision profiles such as small round-disc and slot-insert spacers. We specify the material per profile at tool-cutting.

## Can you make custom spacer moulds from drawings?
Yes. Send a sample photo, dimensions or marked drawing. We cut the steel injection-mould tool in-house and typically ship first-article samples in 15–30 days after drawing approval.

## Can I order different spacer types in one shipment?
Yes. Mixed-SKU orders are common for construction projects where multiple spacer types are required together.

## Are these moulds only for rebar cover?
No. Spacer block moulds are also used for ballast blocks, concrete test specimens and other precast concrete elements.

## Five things that determine the quote — and where custom orders usually go wrong
A custom mould quote is only as good as the input. These are the five points that move price and lead time the most, and the mistakes we see most often from first-time OEM buyers.

- Internal vs external dimensions. Drawings usually specify the finished concrete size (internal clear opening, finished depth). Moulds are cut to the external / as-cast dimension plus wall thickness and draft. If your drawing gives external dimensions only, tell us — otherwise we will build to the wrong number.

- Wall thickness and draft angle. PP and ABS moulds need a draft (taper) to demould without tearing. A 1°–2° draft is normal for block / slab shapes; deeper parts may need more. If the part must have vertical walls (e.g. a tile with zero draft), that pushes us toward a split or multi-piece mould, which costs more and lasts longer.

- Logos, letters and patterns. Embossed text (raised on the concrete) is much cheaper than debossed (engraved) because the mould is machined around the text. Deeply engraved logos, two-level patterns or fine serifs need an etched insert, which adds tooling cost. Send the artwork as AI / DXF / high-resolution PNG.

- Material choice. The default PP mould gives 150+ pour cycles and is the cheapest. If the part is large, thin-walled, or will be used in sub-zero weather, upgrade to ABS or add ribs; choose ABS when the shape needs flex to demould (e.g. some interlocking blocks).

- Sample vs drawing. A dimensioned CAD file is fastest. A photo with sizes written on it works. A physical sample mailed to the factory gives us the best chance to match texture and fit, but adds 5–7 days of courier time. If you have a sample, mail it — and send the drawing in parallel so we can start review.

## Ready for a custom mould review?
Send the drawing or sample photo with target quantity and destination country. We will come back with feasibility, material suggestion, lead time and a budget price range — usually within one working day.

## Custom Precast Moulds — FAQ

## Which file format do you need for a custom mould drawing?
DWG or DXF is preferred. PDF with dimensioned sections, STEP/IGES 3D files, or even a clear photo with sizes written on it in pen also work. For logo and pattern work, send vector artwork (AI / EPS / DXF) or a high-resolution PNG with clean edges.

## Can you make a mould from a physical sample?
Yes. Mail the sample to our Jiaxing factory and we will 3D-scan or hand-measure it, confirm the drawing back to you, then cut the mould. Courier typically takes 5–7 days. Email the tracking number and a photo of the sample so we can start review in parallel.

## What is the difference between PP and ABS moulds?
PP is the default — lowest cost, 150+ pour cycles, slight flexibility for demoulding. ABS is harder, holds tighter tolerances and reproduces finer surface detail (logos, patterns) but is less impact-resistant in cold weather. ABS is the better choice when the part has an undercut or shape that needs the mould to flex during stripping.

## Can you emboss or engrave our company logo, project name or date code?
Yes. Embossed (raised) text and logos are included at low or no cost on most orders. Engraved (recessed) text, two-level patterns, or logos smaller than ~15 mm may need a machined / etched insert and add tooling cost. Send the artwork when you request the quote.

## What is the lead time for a custom mould?
A simple profile change on an existing mould: 10–15 working days. A new shape with no existing tooling: 20–30 working days. Moulds with etched pattern inserts, complex split cavities or large sizes may run longer. The schedule is confirmed in writing after the deposit and drawing sign-off.

## Do you make one-off prototype moulds, or only production quantities?
Single-piece prototype and first-article moulds are accepted. Many customers order one prototype first, pour a test batch, and then release a production order after the part is approved. Prototype moulds use the same material as the production version so the test is representative.

## Can a custom mould be modified later if my dimension changes?
Some changes are possible (welding inserts to reduce a cavity, machining a deeper groove, adding a logo plate). Others are not (making a cavity larger, changing an external footprint, or adding an undercut). Tell us if the design is likely to be revised and we will build in extra stock so the mould can be re-machined.

## How are custom moulds packed for export?
Moulds are stacked on pallets, layered with protective film, and strapped for 20 ft / 40 HC loading. Very large or fragile moulds get plywood crating. We mark each pallet with your PO number, mould dimensions and quantity for site identification. Packing photos are sent before container loading.

## Diamond-Pattern Cover Mould Buyer Guide

Pick the diamond cover by trench class (municipal / sidewalk / railway), then by thickness for the load and PP-or-ABS for the panel size. Tread pattern follows your drawing or authority standard.

## Two cover groups on this page

- Standard municipal (6): 44.4×49.4×3, 54.4×49.4×2.5, 59.4×49.5×6, 49.5×34.5×5 (narrow 35cm-class trench), 54×50×5, 84.4×49.4×3 — roadside, sidewalk and utility trenches.

- Heavy railway (3): 100×50×8, 126×50×8 and 148×50×7 diamond Tie Biao — long-span 7-8cm slabs for railway/HSR cable-trench walkways.

## Three things buyers get wrong

- Choosing by the tread instead of the section. Diamond vs dot vs striped is an anti-slip finish; load is set by thickness and reinforcement. A 2.5cm diamond slab is pedestrian only — trackside trenches need the 7-8cm railway series.

- Cutting a notch on site. If a cable crosses the trench at a cover point, the notch must be moulded — quote notch width × depth and middle/end position with the order; a sawn notch breaks the edge. See notched covers.

- Asking for a 100-148cm slab in PP. Long thin/wide panels warp in PP; the 84cm and 100-148cm slabs run in ABS for a flat panel and clean diamond-rib release. We confirm material by size.

Municipal roadside / sidewalk trench44-59cm diamond covers, 2.5-6cmL×W×T, walking-surface requirement, PP/ABS

Narrow 35cm-class side ditch49.5×34.5×5 narrow diamond slabTrench inner width, seat dimensions, L×W×T

## Diamond-Pattern Drainage Cover Mould FAQ

## What is a diamond-pattern drainage cover mould?
It is a plastic (PP/ABS) injection mould for a precast concrete trench or ditch cover whose top is formed with a raised diamond / rhombus tread (菱形纹). The diamonds interlock into a continuous anti-slip walking surface that drains grit off the raised edges — a common finish on municipal drainage trenches, road shoulders, sidewalks, cable trenches and railway-side walkways. It is the diamond sibling of dot (stud), striped and cobblestone-pattern covers.

## Diamond pattern vs dot pattern — which anti-slip surface should I choose?
Both are anti-slip treads; the difference is visual and project-standard. Dots (圆点) are round raised studs, the dominant choice on railway tunnel cable trenches (see our HST/Tie Biao dot series). Diamonds (菱形) are interlocking rhombus ribs that read as a continuous directional tread, widely specified on municipal roadside and plaza trenches. Performance is set by slab thickness and reinforcement, not by the tread shape — choose the pattern your drawing or authority standard calls for; we make both from the same PP/ABS tooling.

## What sizes are in this diamond-pattern catalogue?
Standard municipal series (6 moulds): 44.4×49.4×3, 54.4×49.4×2.5, 59.4×49.5×6, 49.5×34.5×5 (narrow 35cm-class trench), 54×50×5 and 84.4×49.4×3 (long 84cm slab). Heavy railway series (3 moulds): 100×50×8, 126×50×8 and the 148×50×7 diamond Tie Biao (菱形铁标) railway-standard cover. Length × width × thickness in cm; any other size is made to drawing.

## What is the diamond Tie Biao (菱形铁标) 148×50×7 cover for?
Tie Biao (铁标) means the cover is made to the Chinese railway industry standard rather than to a single project. The 148×50×7 diamond Tie Biao slab — together with the 100×50×8 and 126×50×8 heavy diamond covers — is a long-span, 7-8cm thick section for railway and high-speed-rail cable-trench walkways that run for kilometres beside the track. Long thick slabs span wide trenches and stay walkable for maintenance crews. We can cast your line code, standard number or project mark in the mould.

## Does the diamond pattern affect the cover's load rating?
No — load comes from slab thickness and concrete reinforcement, not from the tread. In this same diamond range you have 2.5-3cm pedestrian covers (54.4×49.4×2.5, 44.4×49.4×3, 84.4×49.4×3) and 7-8cm railway covers (100×50×8, 126×50×8, 148×50×7). We do not label covers with a D/B load class — that is a property of the reinforced concrete you pour, not of the mould; tell us the application (sidewalk / road shoulder / trackside) and we confirm the section thickness.

## Does a diamond-pattern cover need a notch or holes?
Only where the trench demands it. A notch (缺口) is moulded into the edge where a cable or pipe crosses the trench at that cover position — order it with notch width × depth and middle/end position; never cut it on site after casting. Holes are for water-carrying ditches where flow must pass through the slab. The diamond catalogue on this page is solid slabs; for notched or perforated covers see the notched cover range or send your drawing.

## PP or ABS — what are these moulds made from?
Standard municipal diamond covers use PP (polypropylene): 150+ pour cycles, economical for long runs. ABS is chosen for large thin panels and heavy long slabs (the 84cm and 100-148cm pieces) because it holds a flat section without warping and releases the sharper diamond ribs. State PP or ABS, or let us recommend by slab size and thickness.

## MOQ, lead time and how to order?
Catalogue moulds carry no strict MOQ across mixed SKUs; custom project moulds are made to order in roughly 15-30 days after drawing approval. For a quote send the cover L×W×T, the diamond-tread requirement, any notch or holes (size + position), the load/application, the project mark or standard number (e.g. Tie Biao), PP or ABS, quantities and destination port — FOB Ningbo/Shanghai. Fastest way: WhatsApp a photo of the cover you want to match and we confirm the nearest catalogue size or quote an OEM mould.

U-shaped diversion channel moulds for agricultural drainage, road runoff control, garden irrigation and industrial drainage. The smooth U-section improves flow capacity and easy cleaning.

## Drainage Channel Mould Buyer Guide

Use this checklist to match drainage channel, U-drain and cover moulds to your local stormwater project before asking for a quotation.

## Common project choices

- Plain U-shaped diversion channels: open trough flow channels (30–62 cm lengths) for roadside drainage, irrigation ditches and stormwater lines.

- Perforated / notched / coin-pattern slots: 3/5/6/8-hole downspout channels, end-notched connectors and decorative coin-pattern (铜钱) surface channels.

- L-shaped diversion curb & gutter stones: L-section kerb-and-gutter units for residential community perimeter drainage, plain or perforated, with or without side holes.

- Corner & water-stop fittings: inside/outside corner units and curved R50/R100/R150 barrier pieces that complete an L-shaped run.

## Material and design notes

Most drainage mould buyers compare PP and ABS according to concrete part size, expected reuse cycle, demoulding method and budget. For covers with many holes or narrow ribs, the mould structure should leave enough demoulding clearance and avoid weak corners.

- Confirm finished concrete dimensions, not only mould outside size.

- Check whether the cover needs anti-slip texture, logo or drainage slot direction.

- For mixed orders, group U-drains, covers and catch basin parts by project line for easier packing.

Buyer needRecommended mould directionQuote details to prepare

Roadside stormwater drainagePlain U-shaped diversion channel mould plus matching coverChannel length, inner width, depth, wall thickness and cover seat size

Residential community perimeter (against wall/kerb)L-shaped gutter stone mould, perforated or plainLength × wall height × base width, hole count, with/without side drain holes

Downspout / pipe connection points3/5/6/8-hole perforated U-channel or notched connector mouldHole count, hole spacing, slot depth, notch width × depth and open ends

Turns and ends of an L-shaped runInside/outside corner units + curved water-stop barriersCorner size and barrier radius (R50/R100/R150), one mould per radius

Decorative pedestrian drainageCoin-pattern (铜钱) channel mouldOuter size and notch layout; pattern is cosmetic anti-slip surface

## Drainage Mould FAQ

## Can you make diversion channel moulds from samples or drawings?
Yes. Send finished concrete dimensions (inner width × depth × length), wall thickness, hole or notch layout, drawings, sample photos or local standards. We review the mould structure and quote standard or custom production.

## PP or ABS — which material should I choose for diversion channels?
Plain U-channels in normal sizes demould well in PP (lower cost, 150+ pour cycles). ABS is recommended for perforated / multi-hole downspout channels and L-shaped corner pieces: the narrow ribs between holes and the right-angle L-section need higher stiffness to survive repeated demoulding without chipping. Tell us the model and usage; we will suggest the material.

## Are the holes in perforated channels drilled on site?
No. The 3/5/6/8-hole layout is moulded in — the holes form part of the concrete shape. Each hole count is a separate mould, and the spacing/slot depth (e.g. 2 cm slot depth on the 60×30×8 downspout channel) is fixed. Give us your pipe or slot layout first; do not plan to drill cured concrete, which cracks the section.

## How do I specify the notches on notched / coin-pattern flow channels?
End notches (commonly 10×1.5 cm or 15×1.5 cm) let two channel runs connect or let water enter from the side. State notch width × depth and how many ends are open. A notch that is too wide leaves a loose joint; too narrow and the mating channel will not seat. Notched and coin-pattern versions of the same outer size (e.g. 30×30×6 or 60×30×6) are different moulds — order by the surface name printed on the product photo.

## What is the difference between a U-shaped channel and an L-shaped gutter stone?
The U-channel is an open trough for a free-standing drainage line. The L-shaped gutter stone (L型水沟石 / 导流侧石) is an L-section kerb-and-gutter unit: the vertical back wall sits against a wall or road edge and the flat base carries the flow — it is the standard residential-community (小区) perimeter drainage unit. L-shaped pieces are available plain, perforated (6/8-hole downspout versions) or with/without side drain holes.

## How do corner and water-stop pieces work for an L-shaped run?
Inside and outside corner units (30×30×6 for gutter stones, 30×15×6 for residential L-channels) turn a run 90°. Curved water-stop / barrier pieces (内挡水 / 外挡水) are made to fixed radii — commonly R50/R100 for inner barriers and R100/R150 for outer barriers. Like any curved precast part, one mould serves one radius: count inside and outside corners separately per plan, and give the radius when ordering curved barriers.

## What concrete grade and wall thickness are recommended?
C25–C30 concrete with proper vibration and curing works for standard drainage components. Wall thickness (5–8 cm on most U-channels, 6–6.5 cm on L-gutter stones) is driven by backfill / traffic load, not by channel width — roadsides with vehicle load need thicker walls and reinforcement regardless of the hydraulic section.

## Can one shipment mix U-channels, L-gutter stones, corners and covers?
Yes. Mixed-SKU container orders are common for municipal and residential drainage contractors. We recommend grouping components by project line (channel bodies + matched notches/holes + corner pairs + covers) so nothing is missing on site.

## Dot-Pattern Cover Mould Buyer Guide

Pick the dot cover by the trench standard (railway tunnel / Tie Biao / expressway / walkway), then by thickness for the load and PP-or-ABS for the panel size. Notch only where a cable crosses.

## Four cover groups on this page

- Hangshaotai HST tunnel series (11): 42×40×6 to 79.4×49.4×6 high-speed-railway tunnel cable-trench covers, some notched, HST/T2H marks.

- Notched dot covers (5): thin 2.5-3.2cm pedestrian walkway slabs with an edge notch 28×1.5cm for cable crossing, plus the 80×50×8 high-speed-rail notched cover.

- Expressway project (5): Guizhou/Baohu/Wenma and Guiyang-ring covers, thin 2.5-3cm sections mostly in ABS.

- Railway standard (5): Tie Biao slabs incl. 120×49×10 extra-long, Qian-Zhang-Chang and Yu-Huai railway covers, 6-10cm.

## Three things buyers get wrong

- Ordering a 2.5cm walkway slab for a trackside/roadside trench. Pattern does not set load — thickness and reinforcement do. Trackside trenches need the 6-10cm covers; the 2.5-3cm panels are pedestrian only.

- Cutting the notch on site. A notch sawn into a finished cover breaks the studded edge and loses the piece — order it moulded, quoting notch width × depth and middle/end position.

- Asking for a thin 70-80cm panel in PP. Large 2.5-3cm slabs warp in PP; the expressway covers are ABS for a flat panel and sharp stud release. We confirm material by size.

## Dot-Pattern Drainage Cover Mould FAQ

## What is a dot-pattern drainage cover mould?
It is a plastic (PP/ABS) injection mould for a precast concrete trench or ditch cover whose top is formed with a field of raised round studs (圆点). The dots give an anti-slip walking surface and a hard-wearing, easily recognised finish — standard on cable-trench and drainage covers beside railway tunnels, expressways, walkways and maintenance corridors. They are the studded sibling of striped and cobblestone-pattern covers.

## Why are so many dot-pattern covers used on railway and tunnel cable trenches?
Railway and high-speed-railway tunnel cable trenches run for kilometres beside the track and are walked by maintenance staff, so the cover needs a visible anti-slip surface, a long straight section and a project-standard mark. This catalogue is dominated by exactly that tooling: the Hangshaotai high-speed-railway tunnel series (杭绍台, 42×40×6 up to 79.4×49.4×6, some stamped HST-T2H), Tie Biao railway-standard covers (铁标, incl. an extra-long 120×49×10 slab), Qian-Zhang-Chang and Yu-Huai railway covers, and the 80×50×8 high-speed-rail notched dot cover. Send your railway line/standard and drawing for a matched set.

## What do the HST / Tie Biao / project marks on the covers mean?
These are project or standard identifiers cast or printed on the slab: HST marks the Hangzhou-Shaoxing-Taizhou high-speed-railway project (some pieces also carry section codes such as T2H), and Tie Biao (铁标) means the cover is made to the railway industry standard rather than to a single project. Highway pieces carry authority names — Guizhou expressway (贵州高速, ABS), Baohu (保沪), Wenma (文马) and the Guiyang southwest ring. We can form your project name, line code, standard number or logo in the mould; send the mark with the drawing.

## Some of these covers have a notch (缺口) — why?
The edge notch lets a cable or pipe cross the trench at that cover position instead of going under the slab — the cover drops over the crossing line. On this page the notched dot covers include the HST tunnel pieces (notch ~25×1.5cm), the thin 2.5-3.2cm walkway covers (notch 28×1.5cm: 59×50×2.5, 61×49×3.2, 71×49×3.2, 81×49×3.2) and the 80×50×8 high-speed-rail piece. Quote the notch width × depth and its position (middle of a run or at the end); a notch cut on site after casting breaks the edge and ruins the piece. See the full notched range here.

## Thin 2.5-3cm covers vs 6-10cm covers — which do I need?
Thickness follows the load on top, not the pattern. 2.5-3.2cm dot covers (59×50×2.5 through 81×49×3.2, plus the ABS expressway 70×49×2.5/73×49×2.5/78×49×2.5) are pedestrian/maintenance-walkway slabs; the large thin ones are made in ABS so the panel stays straight. 6-10cm covers (the 6cm HST and Tie Biao series, 78×40×7, 80×50×8 and the 120×49×10 extra-long Tie Biao slab) take trackside/roadside and occasional-vehicle loads. Load class is set by thickness and reinforcement — tell us the application and we confirm the section.

## PP or ABS — what are these moulds made from?
Most standard 6cm railway covers use PP, which gives 150+ pour cycles and is the economical choice for long project runs. The thin large panels are typically ABS (e.g. the 70×49×2.5 Guizhou expressway cover) because ABS holds a flat 2.5-3cm section without warping and gives sharper dot texture release; ABS is also chosen for extra-long slabs (120cm) where stiffness matters. State PP or ABS with the inquiry, or let us recommend by size and thickness.

## Can you make dot-pattern covers to our railway or expressway drawing?
Yes — project tooling is a core part of this range. Beyond the catalogue HST, Tie Biao, Qian-Zhang-Chang, Yu-Huai, Guizhou/Baohu/Wenma and Guiyang-ring pieces, we build moulds from customer drawings: send the cover L×W×T, the dot-pattern requirement, any notch (size + position), the load/application, the project mark or standard number, and whether PP or ABS. We confirm mould design, demoulding draft and the matching channel seat before cutting.

## MOQ, lead time and how to order?
Catalogue moulds carry no strict MOQ across mixed SKUs; custom railway/highway project moulds are made to order in roughly 15-30 days after drawing approval. For a quote send the drawing or a marked sample photo, cover quantities, destination port and packing preference — FOB Ningbo/Shanghai. Fastest way: WhatsApp a photo of the cover you want to match (with the project mark if any) and we confirm the nearest catalogue size or quote an OEM mould.

## Material and design notes

Most drainage mould buyers compare PP and ABS according to concrete part size, expected reuse cycle, demoulding method and budget. For covers with many holes or narrow ribs, the mould structure should leave enough demoulding clearance and avoid weak corners.

- Confirm finished concrete dimensions, not only mould outside size.

- Check whether the cover needs anti-slip texture, logo or drainage slot direction.

- For mixed orders, group U-drains, covers and catch basin parts by project line for easier packing.

## Drainage Trench Mould 50×48×38 cm (Inner 30×30) — From Injection to Finished

Trenches are specified by the INNER flow section — inner 30×30 means a 30×30 cm waterway. The external vertical ribs stop the tall walls ballooning under wet concrete, and the cover bearing ledge must match the cover mould.

## Will It Break? Drop & Stomp Test on a PP Drain Trench Mould

A worker stands on, stomps and throws a long trench mould — it bounces, no crack. Moulds fail in the field from demoulding and vibration stress, not static weight: injection PP flexes, which is how it reaches 150+ pour cycles.

## QC-Labelled Drain Trench Moulds Stacked & Truck-Loaded | Blue-Label Batch

Every mould carries a blue QC label with a traceable QR code linking it to its material batch and production run. Long U-trench moulds ship nested and stacked with labels facing out for count-and-check on arrival.

## Assembled Trapezoidal Channel Mould Buyer Guide

Segmental ditch liners — base slab + left/right side slabs + coping — specified by finished cross-section (top opening / base / depth). Match the piece moulds to the ditch size and whether it is free-standing or against a wall.

## Four mould groups on this page

- Assembled sets: complete trapezoidal cross-sections, opening 100–320cm, shown as base + sides + coping (No.1–18, 10-1/10-2, 2025-180A/B, 2025-240, 2025-320).

- Base slabs: single bottom pieces 54.8–72cm and the deep 65×32×19 slab.

- Side slabs & coping: single sloped-wall pieces (56.3, 70.7) and cap stones (50×33 coping).

- L-shaped slabs: one-piece base-and-wall pieces for wall/kerb-edge drains (85×40×39, 74×40×39.5).

## Three things buyers get wrong

- Ordering a one-piece U-channel for a big ditch. Openings over ~100cm are built from assembled base+side+coping pieces; a one-piece trough that large will not demould or ship.

- Forgetting left/right side slabs are handed. A trapezoidal lining needs both a left and a right side-slab mould; they are not interchangeable.

- Reading drafted thickness as a tolerance. Figures like 11.5-8.3cm are a deliberate demoulding taper; wall thickness is set by load, not by the ditch opening.

120–160cm openingNo.1–No.8 sets (base 46–108cm)Opening/base/depth, coping yes/no, R-curve if any

## Assembled Drainage Channel Mould FAQ

## What are assembled / segmental trapezoidal drainage channel moulds?
These moulds cast the separate concrete lining pieces of a trapezoidal farm or roadside drainage ditch: a base slab (底板), two side slabs (边板, the left and right sloped walls) and optional coping / cap stones (帽石) along the top edge. The pieces are precast in the factory and assembled on site to form a lined trapezoidal channel. This is different from a one-piece U-channel mould (see our U-drain channel page), which forms the whole trough in a single pour. Assembled liners are used for larger ditches — top openings from 100cm up to 320cm — where a one-piece mould would be too big to transport and demould.

## How do I specify a set — what do 'opening / base / depth' mean?
Each complete set is defined by its finished trapezoidal cross-section: top opening (上口, the width at the top), base width (下口/底宽, the flat bottom) and depth (深度). For example the 2025-180 set is opening 180cm / base 60cm / depth 60cm; the 2025-240 is opening 240 / base 60 / depth 60; the 2025-320 is opening 320 / base 80 / depth 80. Send the ditch cross-section drawing or these three figures plus the per-piece wall thickness, and we confirm the base-slab, side-slab and coping mould sizes that build it.

## Do I order a 'set' or separate piece moulds?
A run of ditch needs all three piece types: base slabs for the floor, side slabs for the two sloped walls (counted per linear metre of each slope), and coping if the top edge is capped. The set photos show how the pieces fit; the moulds themselves are sold per piece type — e.g. a base-slab mould 68×50×10, a side-slab mould 98×50×10. Order the base mould once and run enough pours for the floor length, plus the side moulds for both slopes, plus the coping mould if used. We can quote the mould kit for a given opening/base/depth and tell you the piece count per metre.

## What is the difference between the 2025-180A and 2025-180B sets?
Both build an opening-180 / base-60 / depth-60cm ditch, but the base slab is designed differently: 180B uses a base slab 68×50×10cm with side slabs 98×50×10, while 180A uses a thicker profiled base 41.5×40×11.5-8.3cm (a drafted section, 11.5 tapering to 8.3) with 40×40×8 side slabs. They are two moulding arrangements for the same finished cross-section — the choice depends on your preferred piece layout and reinforcement. Send the drawing; we match it to A or B rather than assuming.

## Are the side slabs left / right handed?
The trapezoidal side slabs are cast from side-specific moulds — a left-side and a right-side piece meet at the base (the 2025-18 and 2025 sets list 'left side slab' and 'right side slab' separately, e.g. left 58.6×40×10 and right 78.5×40×10). A left piece cannot be used as a right piece. Order both left and right side-slab moulds for a complete lining; the base-slab and coping moulds are not handed.

## What are the L-shaped channel slabs for?
The L-shaped channel slab (L形水沟板, e.g. 85×40×39-10 or 74×40×39.5cm) combines the base and one wall in a single L-section piece — used where the ditch runs against a wall or road edge and only one sloped side is needed, or for small edge drains. It is an alternative to the three-piece trapezoidal set, not a replacement part for it. Tell us if the drain is free-standing (use trapezoidal set) or against a wall/kerb (L-shaped pieces may suit).

## What does '8.3' or a size like '41.5×40×11.5-8.3' mean?
These slabs have a drafted (tapered) wall for demoulding, so the thickness is given as two figures — 11.5cm tapering to 8.3cm on the profiled base, or the standard 8.3cm wall on the 2025 sets. The taper is a designed draft angle, not a tolerance. Single-piece slabs are quoted at their nominal thickness (6, 7, 8, 8.3, 10 or 12cm depending on the ditch size and load). Wall thickness should follow the design load — roadside ditches subject to vehicle load need thicker walls and reinforcement regardless of the hydraulic section.

## What concrete, material and lead time apply?
C25–C30 concrete with vibration and standard curing; larger roadside/road-crossing ditches should be reinforced. The moulds are PP for standard slabs (150+ pours); large or deeply-profiled pieces (the 2025-240/320 thick bases, R100 curved side pieces) suit ABS for stiffer walls. Mixed-SKU orders have no strict MOQ; custom cross-sections are made to order in 15–30 days after drawing approval. Send the ditch cross-section, linear metres, piece layout and destination port for an FOB Ningbo/Shanghai quote.

## See the Finished Product on Site

Precast concrete drain covers cast in our moulds, being installed on a live project. If you want to see a specific mould in use before ordering, ask us — we can usually send footage of the exact design.

## Demoulding and Stacking — and Why Lifting Recesses Matter

Covers coming out of the mould and being stacked by hand. Note the paired pockets in the top face: those are lifting recesses — blind hand-grip pockets, not drainage holes and not through-holes. They are what makes a heavy slab liftable by two people on site. How many pairs you need depends on slab weight, so tell us the cover size and we will advise.

## Slotted Drainage Cover Moulds — 3-Slot Grating Stacked for Order

Three long grating slots pass high surface-water volume at road edges, ramps and garage entrances rather than pedestrian plazas. Slots over ~25–30 mm can catch high heels — tell us where the cover goes and we match the slot width.

## Drainage Mould FAQ

## What concrete grade is recommended?
We recommend C25-C30 concrete with proper vibration and curing for standard drainage components. Heavy-duty covers may require higher grades.

## Can one shipment include covers, channels and catch basins?
Yes. Mixed-SKU orders are common for municipal supply and drainage contractors who need multiple component sizes in one shipment.

## Flat Kerb & Strip Stone Mould Buyer Guide

Flat-laid kerb stones are often confused with upright kerbstones, but they are specified differently. Get these points right and the drainage line will sit flat and flow correctly.

## Typical flat stone types

- Small square flat stones (8–19 cm): footway/courtyard paving and patching; 1-out-5 / 1-out-6 multi-cavity for volume.

- Strip stones (20 cm class, 1-out-2 / 1-out-10): narrow border/edge strips; multi-cavity keeps unit cost low.

- 50 cm flat kerb & gutter strip stones: the standard road module. Narrow 8–12 cm widths sit in the gutter channel; wider 15–16 cm flats form the apron.

- Round-top strip kerbs: a slightly raised rounded edge in the gutter line.

- 71–80 cm apron slabs: wide transition panels around drains and crossings; four-hole versions drain through the slab.

## What to get right when ordering

- Flat-laid vs upright: confirm the unit lies down (flat stone / ping shi) or stands up (kerbstone). A flat stone's third dimension is usually small; a tall 18×30 or 12×30 unit is a standing profile.

- Order by face width for drainage: the gutter strip width sets how much water the channel captures; the apron width sets the transition zone. Send a cross-section.

- Cavities change the price: 1-out-10 makes ten pieces per pour. Compare quotes per finished stone, not per mould.

- Thin veneer slabs are real: 0.5–2 cm thin panels are veneer/wear-course units, not undersized stones.

- Match the apron to the kerb family: flat stones, upright kerbs and covers in one run should share a profile so joints line up.

Kerbstone & Curbstone Moulds →
Drainage Channel / Trench Moulds →
Drainage Cover Moulds →
Concrete Paver Block Moulds →
Flat Kerb & Strip Stone Buying Guide →

## What to send for a fast quote
Flat kerb and strip stone jobs usually follow a road cross-section. A drawing or clear photo of the profile lets us confirm width, thickness, chamfer/bevel, cavities and demoulding direction.

- Finished stone length, face width and thickness/height

- Flat-laid (flat stone) or standing (tall kerb) profile

- Number of cavities wanted (1-out-2 / 1-out-10 for volume)

- Application: gutter channel, apron transition, footway, median or courtyard

- Any project/authority logo and PP or ABS preference

- Quantity, destination country and mixed-SKU requirements

## Flat Kerb & Strip Stone Mould FAQ

## What is a flat kerb stone (ping shi / flat stone) and how is it different from a kerbstone?
A kerbstone (lu yuan shi / curbstone) is the upright road-edge unit that contains traffic and separates road from footway. A flat kerb stone (ping shi, flat stone or side-flat stone) is laid FLAT, typically between the upright kerb and the carriageway or gutter: it forms the smooth apron/transition strip that guides surface water toward the drain. Round-top strip stones and gutter strip stones sit in the same flat-laid drainage line. They are a complementary family, usually ordered together with upright kerbstones.

## How do I read a size like 50 x 15 x 15 cm on a flat kerb stone?
It is length x width (the flat face width) x height/thickness, in centimetres. For flat-laid stones the last figure is usually small (6-21 cm) because the unit lies down; for tall flat kerbs (e.g. 79 x 18 x 30) the last figure is the standing height. On thin veneer slabs such as 18.5 x 18.5 x 0.5 cm, 0.5 cm is the real veneer thickness, not a typo.

## What does 1-out-2, 1-out-6 or 1-out-10 mean?
It is the number of finished pieces one mould casts per pour. A 1-out-10 strip-stone mould makes ten small stones in a single cycle. More cavities mean lower cost per piece and faster output for high-volume items, but the mould is larger. When comparing quotes, check whether the price is per mould or per finished stone.

## Flat kerb stone or gutter strip stone - which do I need next to a drain?
Use a gutter strip stone (the narrow 8-12 cm wide, often deeper units) right at the channel to carry the water, and wider flat kerb apron slabs (up to 48-50 cm wide) as the transition toward the footway or carriageway. Round-top strip stones are used where a slightly raised, rounded edge is wanted in the gutter line. Send a cross-section and we will match the profile.

## Are the big 71-80 cm slabs strong enough as thin as 6-8 cm?
Yes, when cast as precast concrete on a flat vibrating table. These wide apron slabs are flat panels, not beams, and they gain stiffness from their width and the sub-base under them. The mould has stiffening ribs on the outside so it stays flat through casting. Handle and store big slabs flat, not on edge.

## PP or ABS for flat kerb and strip stone moulds?
PP (polypropylene) is the default for high-volume plain flat stones - it flexes under vibration and demoulding and reaches 150+ pour cycles. ABS is chosen where a sharp chamfer, a dished/concave face or a thin crisp arris must stay precise over many cycles; several of our small and 50 cm items are stocked in ABS. Tell us the profile and we will recommend the grade.

## Can you add a project or road-authority logo to the slab?
Yes. We already produce project-marked units (e.g. the 75 x 49 x 8 cm slab with a Guizhou road-bridge authority mark). Four-hole and standard apron slabs can be tooled with your logo or marking from artwork; OEM tooling takes about 10-15 days.

## What is the MOQ and lead time?
Standard catalogue flat kerb, strip stone and apron slab moulds have no strict MOQ and mixed-SKU orders are welcome. Lead time is typically 15-30 days; OEM/profile or logo tooling depends on complexity. Send sizes, quantities and destination port for an FOB Ningbo/Shanghai quote.

## Flat Stone and Notched Cover Mould Buyer Guide

Flat-top covers and notched-seat covers for ditch lines, road shoulders and landscape drainage.

## Four cover families on this page

- Flat stone covers: a plain smooth top face, chosen where the cover should disappear into the paving rather than add texture. From 34×40×5cm walkway covers to 50×50×10cm heavy squares.

- Single-notch covers: a recessed shoulder on one end so the slab drops into the channel edge and sits flush — the 40cm-width series from 40×27×6 up to 47×40×6, plus the wide 70×40×6 span.

- Double-notch covers: shoulders on both ends for long spans that seat on two channel edges, such as 78×40×6cm.

- Handle (grip) covers: a shaped recess in the top face as a hand grip (60×40×8 and 64×40×8cm) for covers lifted regularly for maintenance.

- Size range: 34×40×5cm to 78×40×6cm; 40cm width is the most repeated ditch-line width.

## Why the notch matters for pricing

A notch changes the mould, not just the concrete. The notch must have draft on every face or the cast slab locks in and the corner chips on release. Because of that, a notched version of the same nominal cover size is a different mould, not an option on an existing one.

- Confirm notch dimensions as width × depth, e.g. 15×1.5cm or 25×1.5cm, and say how many ends are notched.

- For handle covers, the grip recess (e.g. 17×2.5cm) needs its own draft so the slab releases cleanly.

- State whether the top face is smooth, or needs a light broom or anti-slip finish.

- For ditch lines, order the U-channel / base slab and the cover as a matched pair so the seat lines up — mismatched mould sets are the most common cause of covers that rock or will not seat.

Buyer needRecommended mould directionQuote details to prepare

Smooth cover flush with pavingFlat stone cover mouldFinished length × width × thickness, surface finish
Cover that seats into a ditch shoulderNotched cover mouldNotch width × depth, number of notched ends
Long span over a wide channelDouble-notched cover mould, 78×40×6cm classClear span, load case, reinforcement
Cover lifted for regular maintenance accessHandle (recessed-grip) cover mould, 60–64×40×8cmGrip recess size, lifting frequency, thickness

## FAQ

## Are flat stone drainage cover moulds only decorative?
No. They are functional concrete drainage covers with a flat, smooth top. The cover carries pedestrian or light-vehicle load and can be cast flush with surrounding paving for a clean finish.

## What is the difference between a flat cover and a notched cover?
A flat cover rests flat on the channel or frame. A notched cover has a recessed shoulder (for example 15×1.5cm or 25×1.5cm) that seats onto the ditch edge or frame lip, so it cannot slide sideways and stays flush. Double-notch covers (78×40×6cm class) seat on both ends for wide spans.

## How do I specify the notch size correctly?
Give the notch as width × depth in cm, and tell us how many ends are notched (one or both). The notch must match your channel shoulder or frame lip — if it is too wide the cover rocks, too narrow and it will not seat. Send a photo of the channel edge if you are unsure.

## What is a handle (recessed-grip) cover mould?
It has a shaped recess in the top face (such as 17×2.5cm) that acts as a hand grip, so maintenance crews can lift the cover without a separate hook. Sizes 60×40×8 and 64×40×8cm are typical for access points that need frequent opening.

## Does thickness matter for drainage covers?
Yes — thickness is driven by load, not by the channel width. 5–6cm covers suit footpaths and landscape ditches; 8–10cm covers suit driveways, plaza edges and maintenance-access lines. The cover also needs steel mesh or rebar inside for vehicle loads; the mould forms the concrete shape but reinforcement is placed during casting.

## Should I order the channel/base slab and cover as a matched pair?
For ditch lines, yes. The cover seat and the channel shoulder have to line up, so order the U-channel or base-slab mould and the cover mould together. Buying them separately from different mould sets is the most common cause of covers that do not seat.

## Can you customize cover size, notch or grip layout?
Yes. Send the finished cover length × width × thickness, the notch or grip drawing, load requirement and a sample photo. We review demoulding (draft angle) feasibility before cutting the mould.

## Which buyers use these moulds?
Precast factories, landscape and municipal contractors, drainage-channel suppliers and ditch-line projects that need concrete cover slabs with a finished top surface — from 34×40cm walkway covers up to 78×40cm double-notch spans.

## Hexagonal Paver Mould Buyer Guide

Hexagon paver moulds are specified as side length × thickness. Thickness is the load decision: 6cm for footpaths, 8–10cm for light vehicles, 12cm and above for heavy or hydraulic works.

## How to choose thickness and face type

- 6cm thickness: footpaths, garden paths and pedestrian-only paving.

- 8–10cm thickness: car parks, driveways and light vehicle traffic — the most ordered range.

- 12–15cm thickness: heavy vehicle aprons, slope surfaces and water-conservancy revetment.

- Anti-slip, concave & convex faces: anti-slip and concave-base types are specified for wet slopes and drainage surfaces; recess depths of 1cm and 2cm are available.

## Project drawing checklist

For hexagonal paver moulds, confirm the side length rather than the across-corners dimension — a 20cm hexagon paver measures 40cm across the diagonal, which is a common source of ordering errors.

- Confirm side length and thickness (e.g. 20×8cm side × thickness).

- State expected traffic load: pedestrian, light vehicle or heavy vehicle.

- Add matching half-hexagon moulds if paving edges must be finished without cutting.

ApplicationSuitable mould typeKey parameters

Footpath / garden pavingFlat hexagon pavers 6cm thickSide length, thickness, surface texture
Car park / drivewayFlat and solid hexagon pavers 8–10cm thickSide length, thickness, chamfer, edge units
Slope & hydraulic worksAnti-slip and concave-base hexagon pavers 12–15cmThickness, face texture, recess depth

## Hexagonal Paver Mould FAQ

## How are hexagonal paver moulds measured?
Hexagonal pavers are specified as side length × thickness. A 20×8cm hexagon paver has 20cm sides and is 8cm thick, which measures about 40cm across the diagonal. Always confirm side length, not the across-corners dimension.

## What thickness of hexagon paver should I choose?
Use 6cm for footpaths and garden paths, 8–10cm for car parks and light vehicle traffic, and 12–15cm for heavy vehicle aprons, slope surfaces and water-conservancy works.

## Do you supply half-hexagon moulds for paving edges?
Yes. We supply matching flat, solid and anti-slip half-hexagon moulds in 17×8, 21×23×8, 25×6, 25×10, 25×12.5, 30×6 and 30×10cm so edges can be finished without cutting full pavers on site.

## What is a 1-out-3 or 1-out-4 hexagon paver mould?
These are multi-cavity moulds that cast three or four small pavers in a single pour. Our 8×5cm 1-out-4 and 9×5cm 1-out-3 moulds are used for small-format decorative paving where labour per unit matters.

# Product: Hollow Hexagonal Revetment Block Moulds
URL: https://zhihuamoulds.com/products/hollow-block-hexagon-moulds

54 sizes 14–25cmWall thickness 3–8.7cmGrass-planting open coresHalf-hexagon edge units

## Moulds for Slope Protection and River Bank Revetment
Hollow hexagonal revetment blocks are the open-cored units laid across embankments, river banks, canal slopes and highway cuttings. The hexagon interlocks on six sides so the mat stays keyed together under water flow, while the open core lets grass root through and turns the slope into vegetated erosion control.
Zhihua supplies 54 hollow hexagonal block mould sizes from 14.5cm to 25cm side length, with wall thickness specified from 3cm up to 8.7cm and tapered wall options for easier demoulding. The range also covers plum-blossom and inner-circle patterns, three-hole units, semi-hollow blocks and half-hexagon moulds for finishing the mat edge.
